mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals monetary easing, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward 20d returns are not significantly higher than baseline when FEDFUNDS declines for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate above 0.3% signals labor market weakening, leading to negative 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20d returns not significantly negative when UNRATE crosses above 0.3pp

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) boosts market confidence, driving positive returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: No significant positive returns when both GDPC1 and INDPRO rise concurrently over 60d

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, high FEDFUNDS rates suppress equity valuations, causing negative 20-day returns.
failure_condition: Positive 20d returns occur when FEDFUNDS >4.5% in a tightening cycle

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected surge in employment (PAYEMS) signals labor market strength, leading to positive returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: No significant positive returns when PAYEMS exceeds 1000 in a month

mechanism_narrative: When both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) simultaneously rise, it indicates a robust economic expansion, driving positive returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: No significant positive returns when both GDPC1 and INDPRO rise concurrently over 20d

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low FEDFUNDS rates signal accommodative policy, boosting equity valuations and positive returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: No significant positive returns when FEDFUNDS <2% in a late-cycle expansion

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in economic output (GDPC1) above 5% suggests strong demand, leading to positive 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20d returns not significantly positive when GDPC1 exceeds 5% in a month
